design:
Use case: precise-object-edit, architectural concept design.
Edit target: the supplied Rhino screenshot. Produce a beautiful landscape architectural concept image from the exact SAME oblique overhead site camera, using only the 3D viewport and omitting the Rhino UI and red circle. Preserve the entire surrounding site's geometry, roads, bridge alignments, existing left island with its saddle mesh canopy and oval atrium, water and existing terrace proportions.
The red circle marks the small elongated mound on the RIGHT, between the diagonal elevated road on its left and the outer curving black road on its right. Design ONLY on this marked mound.
CLIENT CORRECTION: previous designs were too large, cluttered, unimaginative and looked like ordinary fragmented ruins. Start fresh. This is an art-directed study of TWO elegant small sculptural futuristic surface remnants, NOT a dense ruin village. The two new objects together occupy at most 10–15% of the marked mound, and the rest stays predominantly open soft grass. They are roughly HALF the linear size of the big pavilion-like ruins often inserted in such scenes. They must read as intimate human-scale outdoor structures, not buildings.
ARCHITECTURE: begin with excellent original FORM, then show limited ruin. Only TWO coherent, flowing, thin double-curved ivory shell remnants, with beautiful continuous curvature and carefully composed negative space. The original forms are parametric freeform surfaces that once folded from a low floor edge into a protective side screen and a partial shade roof; time has erased most of the upper skin. Their formerly continuous design remains readable. No domes, no conventional arches, no rows of frames, no rectangular rooms, no complete roof, no churches, no ancient stonework, no random disconnected slabs, no rubble piles, no repeated piers, no thick fake rocks.
PRIMARY FORM: an elegant asymmetrical twisted crescent ribbon, approximately 18m long, 10m across, mostly 2–4m tall with a single slender high tip under 5m. It curls from near ground into a tilted double-curved side shell and then sweeps down again, one large flowing slit opens toward the RIGHT. One broad roof portion is completely absent, leaving only THREE graceful slender weathered steel ribs tracing its original curvature. One deliberate fracture interrupts a portion of the upper edge and exposes a thin dark sandwich core. It should feel like a beautiful aerodynamic seashell drawn with one decisive architectural gesture, partially ruined, not a scattered skeleton. Subtle panel seams establish manufactured future technology.
SECONDARY FORM: a separate smaller low folded lens-shaped wind screen, approximately 10m long, 7m across, maximum 3m tall. An elegant sinuous curved wall transitions into a shallow ground-level seating edge; the upper roof is gone. One missing crescent-shaped section and two short exposed ribs establish decay. Keep this second form quieter and lower than the first, but related by the same surface language. At most two broad fallen skin fragments rest quietly near the original edge. Both objects remain roofless and open to the sky.
SCALE AND PLACEMENT: on the final roughly 1690px-wide site image, primary object footprint should be approximately 90–110px wide, secondary approximately 60–80px, separated by a substantial OPEN grass interval. NOT 150–250px wide objects and NOT a continuous settlement filling the mound. Put the primary around the middle/upper part of the marked mound and the second toward the lower/right shoulder, with plenty of untouched terrain around both. A pair of tiny 1.75m human scale silhouettes may clarify that the tallest shell is only about 3 human heights.
VIEW DIRECTION MUST BE RIGHT: the more solid backs of the two shells are on the LEFT, facing the adjacent diagonal road. Their open sides, beautiful framed gaps and subtle floor grooves face toward the RIGHT-HAND lower pale semicircular terrace inside the outer road loop. One restrained curving ground path connects the two forms and drifts toward a small flush viewing edge on the RIGHT. No cantilever decks over the left road, no new bridges, no large observation platforms. Leave the right lower terrace almost entirely EMPTY for future landscape design.
RUIN EXPRESSION: precise large-scale absence, a few fractured shell tips, a few exposed curved ribs, restrained weathered metal and small plants in joints. Avoid turning graceful surfaces into jagged stone ruins. Elegant intentional original geometry must dominate; decay is selective. No ornament or busy greebles.
LIGHTING / STYLE: calm high-quality stylized architectural concept render, matte warm ivory, softly shadowed undersides, muted dark bronze-grey ribs, restrained greens, turquoise water, clean daylight. Low vegetation only along a few edges and cracks; no dense shrubs or tiny scattered debris. Quiet, imaginative, airy, graceful and sculptural, clearly near-future. Existing distant context can remain pale simple CAD-like architecture so the scale and placement are easy to judge.
No captions, red markings, arrows, logos, UI or watermarks.
scale_refinement:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Make ONE strictly localized SCALE CORRECTION to the supplied architectural image.
Preserve the entire image's camera, perspective, landscape, roads, bridge geometry, islands, water and existing structures absolutely unchanged. Preserve the elegant shape language and orientation of the TWO curved shell remnants on the grassy mound at the right. They open toward the RIGHT lower terrace, which remains correct.
ONLY change their scale: both shell remnants, their exposed ribs, their small floor pads and their immediate seating edges must be reduced to approximately 55–60 PERCENT of their present linear dimensions, uniformly in plan AND height, around their respective current floor contact centers. After the change the primary shell's floor footprint should be about 110–120 pixels wide instead of ~210 pixels in the supplied frame; secondary about 75–85 pixels wide instead of ~150 pixels. Keep their general centers in approximately the same places, so substantially more quiet open grass surrounds and separates them. Restore natural continuous grass over the footprint portions no longer occupied. Do NOT enlarge or spread the grass mound or change any road or platform edge to compensate.
Keep the human scale figures at their CURRENT size and ordinary adult height; do not shrink them with the architecture. The highest surviving shell tip should feel only about THREE adult human heights, and the lower shell about TWO. The user explicitly objects to oversized structures. These are intimate open-air outdoor architectural fragments, not large pavilions.
Keep their beautiful smooth off-white double-curved manufactured shells, local missing roof skin and sparse curved steel ribs, and their view openings toward screen right. No new ruin pieces, no new rooms, no added debris, no extra vegetation density. There must still be exactly TWO structures. The light path may narrow into a modest walking trail and adapt around the smaller floor pads, without any grand plaza or wide paved axis.
Lighting, materials, surrounding design and framing unchanged. No annotation, text, arrows, logos, or UI.
